momentum.introduction: This guide explains the Investment Analysis Engine **Momentum Strategy** from an investor/user perspective.

sections.heading: What this strategy does
sections.markdown:
Momentum compares a short [SMA](help:terms/sma) with a longer [SMA](help:terms/sma) over historical closing prices and reports the current relationship plus [crossover](help:terms/crossover) state.

It is a price-series analysis. It does not determine business quality, intrinsic value, or whether a security should be bought or sold.

sections.heading: Default windows
sections.markdown:
The current defaults are:

```text
short window = 50
long window = 200
```

They ship with the application and may be overridden key by key in the strategy's settings file; the keys are `short_window`, `long_window`, `rsi_period` (14) and `history_start_date` (the first day of the price history, 2021-01-01).

The short window must be smaller than the long window.

sections.heading: How the calculation works
sections.markdown:
For a window of `n` observations:

```text
SMA_t(n) = mean(P[t-n+1 : t])
```

The strategy calculates a short moving average and a long moving average over the historical `Close` series, then evaluates their relationship and whether that relationship changed on the latest observation.

A crossover needs two consecutive valid SMA pairs. Having exactly enough prices for the long SMA establishes today's relationship but not a prior relationship; crossover is unavailable in that case. The RSI uses simple trailing averages of gains/losses, as specified in [Financial Math](help:documents/finance-math#momentum-strategy).

The result's technical evidence retains original provider retrieval time and cache origin. Historical daily labels are not verified exchange-close timestamps, and the provider's past adjusted-price vintages are not retained. Observation-date filtering alone is not a guarantee of historical knowability. Missing or nonfinite prices cause a failure with the affected field/date when known; the application does not silently remove bad rows or substitute an older close.

In investor terms:

- short SMA above long SMA → bullish price-momentum state;
- short SMA not above long SMA → bearish price-momentum state under the current rule;
- transition into the bullish relationship → bullish crossover;
- transition out of the bullish relationship → bearish crossover.

See [Financial Math](help:documents/finance-math#momentum-strategy) for the exact deterministic convention.

sections.heading: Point-in-time analysis and cache control
sections.markdown:
Only price observations at or before the as-of boundary are used. The boundary is a date or a timezone-aware timestamp. A run can bypass historical price cache reads and writes.

The result reports the latest observation that remained after the boundary was applied, not the boundary you requested. A date-only boundary includes that whole day.

`data_as_of` and each price observation's `observed_at` are exchange-local trading dates. A daily series stamped at local midnight in its own timezone is read by those local calendar dates, so each observation is reported as that date at 00:00 UTC, the same form a timezone-naive series produces, and a date-only as-of boundary includes the bars dated on or before that date in the exchange's calendar. A series with any bar at another time of day keeps the exact instants its provider supplied. One case is not corrected: a daily bar stamped as the UTC instant of a non-UTC local midnight (for example 15:00 UTC for a Tokyo date), because the series does not carry the exchange's timezone.

As-of runs fetch history only up to the boundary, so they are cached separately from live runs, and an invalid price dated after the boundary does not affect them. The one exception is a provider that stamps a daily price later in its date than the boundary time; Yahoo stamps daily prices at midnight, so it does not apply to them.

Provider-adjusted prices are revised retroactively: splits and dividends restate history. An as-of result is therefore filtered to a date but reflects today's adjusted view of the prices on that date, not the prices as they would have looked then. See [look-ahead bias](help:terms/look-ahead-bias).

Bypassing the cache affects the historical price cache only. A saved run stores the as-of and cache choices with the run, and refreshing a watchlist entry saved this way reuses them.

sections.heading: Sufficient history is required
sections.markdown:
A moving average cannot be calculated until enough price observations exist for its window.

If the returned history is too short, the strategy reports the affected values/result as unavailable or unknown rather than pretending that missing values are zero. A history too short for the long average gives a trend of `UNKNOWN` and the status `input_unavailable`. The RSI is still calculated and shown when the history is longer than the RSI period.

Machine-readable JSON uses `null` for unavailable numeric outputs rather than non-standard `NaN`.

sections.heading: Statuses and failures
sections.markdown:
Every Momentum result carries a status, as the other strategies' results do:

| Situation | Status | Run outcome |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A bullish or bearish trend | `ok` | `completed` |
| The history is too short for the long average (trend `UNKNOWN`) | `input_unavailable` | `unavailable` |
| No price history exists at or before the as-of boundary | `input_unavailable` | `unavailable` |
| The price data failed a data-quality check | `input_unavailable` | `unavailable` |
| The price provider failed | `provider_error` | `failed` |

A result that could not be calculated has a reason, and a reason code where one fits (`insufficient_history`, `not_available_as_of` or `provider_error`; a failed data-quality check has the reason only). A provider failure never stores the provider's own error text: the stored reason is a fixed message, and `provider_failure` names the provider and the kind of failure.

A saved run keeps a failed or unavailable outcome, and refreshing a watchlist entry records it as a run with that outcome instead of an error without a run.

sections.heading: Data source
sections.markdown: Momentum currently obtains historical market-price data from Yahoo Finance through the third-party [`yfinance`](https://ranaroussi.github.io/yfinance/) library and operates on the normalized historical `Close` values returned to the strategy. `yfinance` is not affiliated with or endorsed by Yahoo.

sections.heading: Why another momentum calculation may disagree
What this strategy does not currently implement
sections.markdown:
The current Momentum strategy is specifically an SMA/crossover analysis, reporting [RSI](help:terms/rsi) as a supporting indicator (see [above](help:documents/momentum#how-the-calculation-works) for its simple-average, not-Wilder-smoothing convention). It does not currently implement [MACD](help:terms/macd), Sharpe ratio, or a 12-month-minus-1-month momentum factor.

Those are separate analytical methods; they should not be inferred from the generic word “momentum.”

sections.heading: Important limitations
sections.markdown:
SMA/crossover analysis is backward-looking. It can lag rapid price changes, produce whipsaws in sideways markets, and says nothing by itself about valuation, balance-sheet quality, earnings durability, or future returns.

Nothing produced by this strategy is investment advice.

piotroski.introduction:
This implementation follows the Piotroski nine-test structure but substitutes the net change in split-adjusted shares outstanding for the original equity-issuance signal, because issuance cannot be established reliably from structured filings.

The Piotroski F-Score is a deterministic financial-strength screen. It runs nine pass/fail tests on a company's reported financial statements for three consecutive fiscal years and counts the tests passed. The result is a score from 0 to 9, not a valuation, a forecast or an investment recommendation.

sections.heading: What the strategy calculates
sections.markdown:
The strategy reads the statements from SEC EDGAR, finds the company's latest annual report at the boundary and scores that year against the two years before it.

Year *t* is the fiscal year of the latest annual report at the boundary; *t−1* and *t−2* are the two years before it. Each test is a strict comparison on unrounded values:

| # | Group | Test | Passes when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Profitability | Positive ROA | net income of *t* ÷ total assets at *t−1* is greater than zero |
| 2 | Profitability | Positive CFO | operating cash flow of *t* ÷ total assets at *t−1* is greater than zero |
| 3 | Profitability | Improving ROA | ROA of *t* is greater than ROA of *t−1* |
| 4 | Profitability | Cash exceeds income | operating cash flow of *t* is greater than net income of *t* |
| 5 | Leverage and liquidity | Falling leverage | long-term debt ÷ average total assets fell, or long-term debt is zero in both years |
| 6 | Leverage and liquidity | Improving liquidity | the current ratio at *t* is greater than at *t−1* |
| 7 | Leverage and liquidity | No dilution | shares outstanding at *t* are not more than at *t−1* |
| 8 | Efficiency | Improving margin | gross margin of *t* is greater than that of *t−1* |
| 9 | Efficiency | Improving turnover | sales ÷ total assets at the start of the year is greater than the year before |

An unchanged ratio earns no point in any test but 5 (zero debt) and 7. See [Financial Math & Data Conventions](help:documents/finance-math#piotroski-f-score-strategy) for the normative definitions, the conventions the method fixes and the edge-case rules.

sections.heading: Reading the result
sections.markdown:
```text
Apple Inc. (AAPL) — Piotroski F-Score: 7 of 9 (complete)
Fiscal year-end: 2024-09-28 · 10-K 0000320193-24-000123 · us-gaap
Industry class: manufacturer (SIC code as filed)
Profitability
  1 Positive ROA          pass         ROA 26.59% > 0
  2 Positive CFO          pass         CFO / assets 33.54% > 0
  3 Improving ROA         fail         ROA 26.59%, prior 27.50%
  4 Cash exceeds income   pass         CFO 118,254,000,000 USD > net income 93,736,000,000 USD
Leverage and liquidity
  5 Falling leverage      pass         long-term debt / assets 26.94%, prior 29.80%
  6 Improving liquidity   fail         current ratio 0.87x, prior 0.99x
  7 No dilution           pass         shares 15,116,786,000, prior 15,550,061,000
Efficiency
  8 Improving margin      pass         gross margin 46.21%, prior 44.13%
  9 Improving turnover    pass         asset turnover 1.11x, prior 1.09x
```

Percentages and multiples are shown with two decimals; when two compared values would look equal at two decimals but differ, both are shown with more digits so the comparison can be seen.

sections.heading: Complete and partial scores
sections.markdown:
A score is **complete** when all nine tests could be decided. A test that cannot be decided is **unavailable**, never a fail: its line shows `unavailable` and the reason. A score is **partial** when six to eight tests are available, and it is always shown as "*x* of *n*" with the unavailable tests named, never as a bare number and never as "*x* of 9":

```text
MNST — Piotroski F-Score: 5 of 6 (partial: tests 1, 3, 4 unavailable)
Fiscal year-end: 2025-12-31 · 10-K 0001104659-26-020831 · us-gaap
Industry class: manufacturer (SIC code as filed)

Profitability
  1 Positive ROA          unavailable  Net income for 2025-12-31 is unavailable: The filings report none for that fiscal year.
  2 Positive CFO          pass         CFO / assets 27.18% > 0
  3 Improving ROA         unavailable  Net income for 2025-12-31 is unavailable: The filings report none for that fiscal year.
  4 Cash exceeds income   unavailable  Net income for 2025-12-31 is unavailable: The filings report none for that fiscal year.
Leverage and liquidity
  5 Falling leverage      pass         long-term debt / assets 0.00%, prior 4.30%
  6 Improving liquidity   pass         current ratio 3.70x, prior 3.32x
  7 No dilution           fail         shares 978,113,000, prior 973,079,000
Efficiency
  8 Improving margin      pass         gross margin 55.85%, prior 54.04%
  9 Improving turnover    pass         asset turnover 1.07x, prior 0.77x

Note: The usual reading of high and low scores applies to complete scores only.
Source: SEC EDGAR; latest evidence available 2026-02-27
Limitation: Follows the Piotroski nine-test structure, with the net change in shares outstanding in place of the paper's equity-issuance test; not an investment recommendation.
```

The title shows the instrument name before the ticker, as in "Apple Inc. (AAPL)", when the instrument profile gives one; the example above shows the ticker alone because no profile is attached to it.

With fewer than six available tests there is no score. The usual reading of the scale applies to complete scores only: a high score (8 or 9) is conventionally read as financial strength and a low score (0 or 1) as weakness. A partial score gets a note saying so and is not ranked against complete scores.

In a side-by-side comparison of runs the strategy offers two cells, **Score** ("7 of 9", or "5 of 6" for a partial score) and **Completeness** ("complete" or "partial (1, 3, 4 unavailable)"), with the fiscal year-end and the filing's taxonomy.

The strategy scores only the latest annual report at the boundary. If that year's inputs are missing, the affected tests are unavailable; an older year is never scored in its place.

sections.heading: Industry class
sections.markdown: The industry class comes from the SIC code on the annual report the score rests on, as filed, never from the company's current code. The F-Score was designed for non-financial firms, so a financial issuer is scored with a warning: its gross-margin and current-ratio tests are typically unavailable. If the class cannot be established, the strategy still runs and a warning says why. When the annual report is stale, the next one being overdue at the as-of date and none filed, the score and its status do not change; a warning gives the fiscal year, the form and the latest date the next report was due, and the anchor filing is shown with the result (see [anchor filing](help:terms/anchor-filing)). An ETF is not scored: the run is reported as not applicable.

sections.heading: Data sources
sections.markdown: All inputs come from SEC EDGAR structured filings: balance-sheet values at three fiscal year-ends, annual income and cash-flow values for two, common shares outstanding at two year-ends and the as-filed SIC code. The fiscal year-ends are found from the periods the filings report, not from filing dates. A company filing under IFRS has no long-term-debt mapping, so test 5 is unavailable for it. The strategy uses no market data and no quote.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.markdown:
- **Dilution is net.** Test 7 compares share counts. A company can issue shares and still pass when buybacks exceed issuance, as Apple did in fiscal 2024. The two counts are compared only when both come from the same filing and the same path, so a company whose prior-year count comes from an earlier filing has test 7 unavailable.
- **Net income is as reported.** The paper uses income before extraordinary items; net income is the modern equivalent. A company that does not tag net income has tests 1, 3 and 4 unavailable.
- **A screen, not a recommendation.** A pass or fail on a test is a statement about reported statements, not about price, scarcity or durability.

piotroski.title: Piotroski F-Score Strategy

groups.title: Free Cash Flow & Earnings Growth Strategy terms

aaa-corporate-bond-yield.body: No live series is currently integrated, so the strategy takes a yield you supply. A future provider integration must retain exact series, units, observation/publication date, and rating/maturity scope.
aaa-corporate-bond-yield.definition: The yield on a documented series of highest-rated corporate debt, used by the Graham Growth Value strategy.
aaa-corporate-bond-yield.name: AAA Corporate Bond Yield

aaa-rating.body: The precise label and methodology depend on the rating agency or published series.
aaa-rating.definition: The highest credit-rating category in commonly used rating scales, indicating very low assessed credit risk.
aaa-rating.name: AAA

accounting-scope.body: The scope is recorded with the figure, so a consolidated figure is not mistaken for a parent-company or segment figure.
accounting-scope.definition: Whether a financial figure covers the whole consolidated group, the parent company alone, or one segment of the business.
accounting-scope.name: Accounting Scope

analysis-run.body: A run is saved when you ask for it, and a refresh saves one for every entry it runs. Showing a saved Analysis Run always replays its own captured evidence; it never re-fetches data or recalculates, so it keeps showing the same result even if a data provider or your configuration changes afterward.
analysis-run.definition: One saved record of a single analysis attempt: the method, the ticker, the exact configuration used and the result, or the fact that no result could be produced.
analysis-run.name: Analysis Run

analysis-strategy.body:
A strategy never leaves a calculation to an AI model. This glossary and the guides call the idea an analysis strategy.

Related terms: [method](help:terms/method), [typed evidence](help:terms/typed-evidence).
analysis-strategy.definition: A rule-based way of analyzing a security, with its own inputs, calculation and way of reading the result. The same inputs always give the same result.
analysis-strategy.name: Analysis Strategy

analyst-consensus-estimate.body: The Free Cash Flow & Earnings Growth contract can carry compatible FY1/FY2 diluted-EPS consensus as optional evidence, but the current production SEC mapping may not provide it. Such evidence requires verified field meaning, forecast horizon, provenance, update behavior, and licensing; the software does not invent it.
analyst-consensus-estimate.definition: An aggregation of forecasts from multiple analysts.
analyst-consensus-estimate.name: Analyst Consensus Estimate

anchor-filing.body: The engine reads the annual reports filed by the as-of date from the newest. The first original report (not an amendment) fixes the fiscal year, and the anchor filing is the newest filing for that year, so an amendment of that year can be the anchor and an amendment of an older year never is. The anchor filing is **stale** when the next annual report was overdue at the as-of date and none had been filed: the as-of date is after the latest date it was due, counted from the fiscal year-end and never from the filing date. The engine never warns early. See [fiscal year](help:terms/fiscal-year), [as-of date](help:terms/as-of-date) and [stale anchor](help:terms/reason-stale-anchor).
anchor-filing.definition: The annual report an analysis rests on: the newest annual report the company had filed by the as-of date, for its newest completed fiscal year. Its fiscal year-end is the date every input is taken at.
anchor-filing.name: Anchor Filing

applicability-status.body: Investment Analysis Engine uses machine-readable statuses including `ok`, `not_applicable`, `input_unavailable`, `invalid_input`, and `provider_error`.
applicability-status.definition: Whether a method can be meaningfully calculated for a security, instead of forcing every security into a numeric result.
applicability-status.name: Applicability Status

as-filed-sic-code.body: A historical analysis therefore sees the code the issuer had then (`ASSIGNED-SIC`). The code shown for an issuer on the SEC website today can differ, and is never used in its place. When the header cannot be read, the [industry class](help:terms/industry-class) is unknown.
as-filed-sic-code.definition: The four-digit industry code that the SEC header of an annual filing assigns to the issuer on the filing date. It is read from the filing an analysis is anchored to.
as-filed-sic-code.name: As-Filed SIC Code

as-of-date.body:
A requested analysis boundary (`as_of`) prevents the resolver from using observations or information that became available after that date.

Related terms: [UTC](help:terms/utc), [data vintage](help:terms/data-vintage).
as-of-date.definition: The time boundary for an analysis or an input: information that became available after that date is not used.
as-of-date.name: As-of Date

asset-turnover.definition: In the F-Score, a year's sales divided by total assets at the start of that year.
asset-turnover.name: Asset Turnover

availability-date.body: Historical analysis must therefore not treat the period-end value as if it had already been published.
availability-date.definition: The date a fact became knowable to an investor. A financial statement's fiscal-period end can precede its filing date by weeks or months.
availability-date.name: Available At / Filing Date / Publication Date

base-pe.definition: The no-growth earnings multiple used as a configurable constant in the selected growth-value convention.
base-pe.name: Base P/E

baseline-aaa-yield.body: It is configurable formula normalization, not a current market observation.
baseline-aaa-yield.definition: The reference AAA yield, 4.4 by default, that the Graham Growth Value formula compares the current AAA yield against.
baseline-aaa-yield.name: Baseline AAA Yield

basic-and-diluted-eps.body: Values with different share bases must not be combined silently.
basic-and-diluted-eps.definition: Basic EPS divides profit by the weighted-average common shares actually outstanding. Diluted EPS also counts potentially dilutive securities such as options and convertible instruments.
basic-and-diluted-eps.name: Basic EPS / Diluted EPS

book-value.body: It may differ greatly from market value and may not capture internally generated intangible assets.
book-value.definition: The accounting value of assets minus liabilities attributable to the relevant equity holders.
book-value.name: Book Value

bvps.body: When using SEC EDGAR data, Investment Analysis Engine derives it from eligible fiscal-year-end balance-sheet components rather than claiming a direct SEC BVPS field.
bvps.definition: Book value attributable to common shareholders divided by period-end common shares outstanding. It is an accounting measure of net assets per share, not a market price.
bvps.name: BVPS (Book Value Per Share)

cache.body:
Otherwise the engine asks an allowed provider or reports the input unavailable. Caching is automatic and distinct from saving an [Analysis Run](help:terms/analysis-run), which is optional and durable.

Related terms: [cache states](help:terms/cache-states).
cache.definition: A stored copy of previously retrieved data. A stored value is reused only if it satisfies the requested as-of date and the freshness policy.
cache.name: Cache

cache-states.body: A stale cache entry exists but is too old or otherwise outside the active policy, so it cannot silently be treated as current.
cache-states.definition: A cache hit finds a valid stored value to reuse, a cache miss finds none, and a stale entry exists but is too old to be treated as current.
cache-states.name: Cache Hit / Cache Miss / Stale Cache Entry

cagr.body:
```text
(ending_value / beginning_value)^(1 / years) - 1
```

A historical EPS CAGR describes the past. It is only a proxy—not a forecast—unless a separate justified policy says otherwise.
cagr.definition: The constant annual rate that would turn a beginning value into an ending value over a stated number of years.
cagr.name: CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate)

capex-sign-convention.body: The engine records the convention so that free cash flow subtracts spending once, whichever sign the provider used. When the convention is missing the figure is ambiguous and is not used. See [capital expenditures](help:terms/capital-expenditures) and [free cash flow](help:terms/free-cash-flow).
capex-sign-convention.definition: How a data provider writes capital expenditures: as a positive amount of spending or as a negative cash outflow.
capex-sign-convention.name: Capital Expenditure Sign

capital-expenditures.body:
Provider sign conventions differ, so Investment Analysis Engine normalizes CapEx to a positive expenditure amount and retains the transformation in provenance.

From SEC filings the engine uses purchases of property and equipment, or, for a filer that reports only the broader purchases of productive assets, that concept. It uses one of the two for a company, never both. The broader concept includes intangible assets such as software, and a result that uses it says so.
capital-expenditures.definition: Cash spent to acquire or improve long-lived productive assets.
capital-expenditures.name: Capital Expenditures (CapEx)

classification-basis.body: The total is the default (`total_fcf`) and the per-share measure is the alternative (`fcf_per_share`). Both measures remain visible regardless of the choice.
classification-basis.definition: The free-cash-flow measure whose growth rate controls the growth screen: the total measure or the per-share measure.
classification-basis.name: Classification Basis

common-shareholders-equity.definition: The part of reported equity that belongs to common shareholders, after the claims of preferred shareholders and other senior equity interests are excluded where applicable.
common-shareholders-equity.name: Common Shareholders' Equity

complete-and-partial-score.body:
A partial score is shown with the unavailable tests named, the usual reading of high and low scores does not apply to it, and it never enters a ranking.

The values are explained in [Complete Score](help:terms/score-complete), [Partial Score](help:terms/score-partial).
complete-and-partial-score.definition: A complete score rests on all nine tests. A partial score rests on six to eight, because the other tests are unavailable.
complete-and-partial-score.name: Complete Score / Partial Score

crossover.body:
The current implementation derives a binary `short_sma > long_sma` signal and differences it to identify transitions.

Both averages must exist at two consecutive observations. The first valid pair can establish trend but cannot establish a crossover. A zero crossover is a verified absence of transition, distinct from unavailable history.

The latest signal is one of three states: a bullish crossover, where the short average moved above the long one; a bearish crossover, where it moved below; or no new crossover, where neither happened.

The values are explained in [Bullish Crossover](help:terms/crossover-bullish), [Bearish Crossover](help:terms/crossover-bearish), [No New Crossover](help:terms/crossover-none).
crossover.definition: A change in which of the short and long moving averages is higher.
crossover.name: Crossover

crossover-bearish.body: It needs two consecutive valid pairs of averages. See [Crossover](help:terms/crossover) for the whole set of values.
crossover-bearish.definition: The relationship moved out of the bullish one since the previous observation: the short moving average stopped being above the long one.
crossover-bearish.name: Bearish Crossover

crossover-bullish.body: It needs two consecutive valid pairs of averages. See [Crossover](help:terms/crossover) for the whole set of values.
crossover-bullish.definition: The relationship moved into the bullish one since the previous observation: the short moving average rose above the long one.
crossover-bullish.name: Bullish Crossover

crossover-none.body: It is a verified absence of transition, which differs from history too short to tell. See [Crossover](help:terms/crossover) for the whole set of values.
crossover-none.definition: Neither a bullish nor a bearish transition happened at the latest observation.
crossover-none.name: No New Crossover

current-aaa-yield.body: It is a value you supply and is identified as such; a future provider-resolved value would additionally need series provenance and observation/publication dates.
current-aaa-yield.definition: The AAA corporate-bond yield used in the denominator of the growth-value formula. It must be strictly positive.
current-aaa-yield.name: Current AAA Yield

current-quote.body:
For an analysis with an explicit historical [as-of date](help:terms/as-of-date), a quote is usable only if the selected provider can establish an eligible observation at or before that boundary. A current-only quote adapter therefore returns unavailable for historical financial-fact requests rather than substituting today's price.

The report calls this the latest available quote. Retrieval time records when the provider response was obtained; market observation time records when the market price was observed, if actually supplied. A five-minute response-reuse bound does not prove that the underlying trade is five minutes old. The current Yahoo adapter retains retrieval time and explicitly reports unknown market observation time.
current-quote.definition: A market price taken as of now, used for comparison with a valuation. For a historical as-of date, it is usable only if the provider can establish a price at or before that date.
current-quote.name: Current Quote / Current Market Price

current-ratio.definition: Current assets divided by current liabilities at a fiscal year-end.
current-ratio.name: Current Ratio

data-provider.definition: An external or local source of market prices, company financial facts or economic-series observations. Examples are a quote service, a financial-statements service and a macroeconomic data service.
data-provider.name: Data Provider

data-vintage.body: A reproducible historical analysis may therefore need the original vintage rather than today's revised value.
data-vintage.definition: The version of a time-series observation that was available at a particular time. Some economic data are revised after first publication.
data-vintage.name: Data Vintage

defensive-investor.body: His complete defensive-stock framework included additional size, financial-strength, earnings-stability, dividend, and growth criteria beyond the two ratios represented by the Graham Number.
defensive-investor.definition: Graham's term for an investor seeking a relatively conservative, low-maintenance approach.
defensive-investor.name: Defensive Investor

discount-and-premium.definition: A neutral description of the same price comparison as margin of safety. A discount means the price is below the reference value; a premium means it is above it.
discount-and-premium.name: Discount / Premium to Reference Value

ebitda.body: The amortization and depreciation come from the cash-flow statement. Lease cost sits above or below EBITDA according to the accounting framework, so a US GAAP and an IFRS filer are not fully comparable.
ebitda.definition: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, taken here as reported operating income plus depreciation and amortization.
ebitda.name: EBITDA

edgar.body: See the SEC's [EDGAR search resources](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings) and [Accessing EDGAR Data](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/accessing-edgar-data).
edgar.definition: The SEC's Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval system, which gives public access to company filings and structured filing data.
edgar.name: EDGAR

ema.body: It is not currently part of the implemented Momentum calculation.
ema.definition: A moving average that gives more weight to recent observations than an SMA does.
ema.name: EMA (Exponential Moving Average)

enterprise-value.definition: Market capitalization plus total debt, preferred stock and noncontrolling interest, minus cash and short-term investments. It may be negative.
enterprise-value.name: Enterprise Value (EV)

entry.body: A [watchlist](help:terms/watchlist) is an ordered list of entries, not a separate list of tickers and a separate list of [selections](help:terms/selection). Each entry's position in the list is a number counted from 1.
entry.definition: One ticker paired with one selection inside a watchlist. The same method can appear in several entries, for different tickers or for one ticker with different configuration.
entry.name: Entry

eps.body: Its basis and period must always be identified.
eps.definition: Profit attributable to common shareholders, expressed per common share. It may be basic or diluted and may cover a fiscal year or a trailing period.
eps.name: EPS (Earnings Per Share)

eps-basis.body: The three-year average smooths a single unusual year. The fiscal-year basis uses one year's earnings as reported. See [three-year-average EPS](help:terms/three-year-average-eps) and [fiscal year](help:terms/fiscal-year).
eps-basis.definition: Which earnings figure a valuation uses: the three-year average, or the earnings of one completed fiscal year.
eps-basis.name: EPS Basis

expected-growth-rate.body: It is written `g` in the formula, and its policy must be reported.
expected-growth-rate.definition: The assumed annual earnings-growth rate used by the Graham Growth Value strategy, in percentage points: 6.5 means 6.5%. Its source and horizon must be reported.
expected-growth-rate.name: Expected Growth Rate

f-score.body: It is shown as “*x* of *n*” with *n* the tests that could be decided, and is unavailable with fewer than six decided tests.
f-score.definition: The number of the nine Piotroski tests passed, from 0 to 9.
f-score.name: F-Score

failure-category-error.body: The other category is [input unavailable](help:terms/status-input-unavailable). A failure the engine cannot place is treated as this category.
failure-category-error.definition: The category of a failure that is not about unusable data. The failure code says what went wrong.
failure-category-error.name: Error Category

failure-configuration-error.body: The message is written for the person who runs the engine.
failure-configuration-error.definition: A setting of the engine prevents the analysis. The message says what to change.
failure-configuration-error.name: Configuration Error

failure-database.definition: The local database could not be used. The code says whether it needs an upgrade, is busy, cannot be read or written, or could not be set up.
failure-database.name: Database Failure

failure-execution-error.body: It is the code used for any failure that no other code describes.
failure-execution-error.definition: The analysis failed in a way the engine did not anticipate. The details are in the engine's log, not in the message shown.
failure-execution-error.name: Unexpected Failure

failure-historical-quality.body: The check names what was wrong with the data. It is not a provider outage: the provider answered, and the answer was rejected. Its category is [input unavailable](help:terms/status-input-unavailable).
failure-historical-quality.definition: The price history failed the engine's data-quality checks, so it was not used.
failure-historical-quality.name: Historical Data Quality Failure

failure-invalid-parameter.body: Nothing was calculated or saved. Correct the named value and ask again.
failure-invalid-parameter.definition: A value in the request, such as a ticker, a date or a window, was rejected before any analysis ran. The message names what was wrong.
failure-invalid-parameter.name: Invalid Parameter

failure-name-conflict.body: Choose another name, or change the existing watchlist.
failure-name-conflict.definition: A watchlist with that name already exists, so the name cannot be used again.
failure-name-conflict.name: Name Already in Use

failure-no-eligible-observations.body: Asking for a date earlier than the first available data gives this failure. Its category is [input unavailable](help:terms/status-input-unavailable). See [as-of date](help:terms/as-of-date).
failure-no-eligible-observations.definition: No observation exists at or before the requested date, so the analysis has nothing to start from.
failure-no-eligible-observations.name: No Eligible Observations

failure-not-found.body: Check the identifier. A refresh job exists only while the server that started it runs.
failure-not-found.definition: The watchlist, entry, saved run, refresh job, help term, help document or address that was asked for does not exist.
failure-not-found.name: Not Found

failure-port-unavailable.body: Choose another port, or stop whatever is using this one.
failure-port-unavailable.definition: The local interface could not start, because the network port it was asked to use is not available.
failure-port-unavailable.name: Port Unavailable

failure-refresh-running.body: Wait for it to finish or stop it, then start the next one. See [refresh](help:terms/refresh).
failure-refresh-running.definition: A refresh is already running, and only one runs at a time.
failure-refresh-running.name: Refresh Already Running

failure-request-refused.body: The interface answers only the application that started it, on this computer.
failure-request-refused.definition: The local interface refused the request, because it carried no valid token or came from a host or origin that is not allowed.
failure-request-refused.name: Request Refused

failure-stored-data-unreadable.body: A saved run may be malformed or may not match its summary. A watchlist entry's saved selection may be unreadable. A saved run may also have no replay in this version.
failure-stored-data-unreadable.definition: A saved run or watchlist entry cannot be read by this version of the engine, so it cannot be shown or replayed.
failure-stored-data-unreadable.name: Stored Data Unreadable

failure-unsupported-run-version.body: The run stays in the database and is refused by its version; it is never read as if it were current.
failure-unsupported-run-version.definition: A saved run was stored under an older version of its shape or method than this version of the engine reads.
failure-unsupported-run-version.name: Unsupported Run Version

failure-watchlist-empty.body: Add an entry first. See [watchlist](help:terms/watchlist) and [refresh](help:terms/refresh).
failure-watchlist-empty.definition: The watchlist has no entries, so there is nothing to refresh.
failure-watchlist-empty.name: Empty Watchlist

fcf-classification.body:
`PASS` means required growth rates are positive; `FAIL` means complete, meaningful evidence includes a nonpositive required rate; `INDETERMINATE` means the required classification cannot be made from admissible evidence. These are distinct from software execution status.

The values are explained in [FCF Growth Pass](help:terms/fcf-growth-pass), [FCF Growth Fail](help:terms/fcf-growth-fail), [FCF Growth Indeterminate](help:terms/fcf-growth-indeterminate).
fcf-classification.definition: The growth screen's three outcomes: pass when required growth rates are positive, fail when complete evidence shows a nonpositive rate, indeterminate when no classification can be made.
fcf-classification.name: FCF Classification

fcf-growth-fail.body: It is a screen result, not a valuation or a recommendation. See [FCF Classification](help:terms/fcf-classification) for the whole set of values.
fcf-growth-fail.definition: The screen fails: a historical growth rate of free cash flow or diluted EPS is zero or negative, or, under the hard gate, forward consensus growth is not positive in both years.
fcf-growth-fail.name: FCF Growth Fail

fcf-growth-indeterminate.body: It is not a failed screen: the engine cannot make the classification from the evidence it may use. See [FCF Classification](help:terms/fcf-classification) for the whole set of values.
fcf-growth-indeterminate.definition: The screen cannot be decided, because a required growth rate could not be calculated or is not meaningful, or the hard gate lacks complete consensus evidence.
fcf-growth-indeterminate.name: FCF Growth Indeterminate

fcf-growth-pass.body: It is a screen result, not a valuation or a recommendation. See [FCF Classification](help:terms/fcf-classification) for the whole set of values.
fcf-growth-pass.definition: The growth screen passes: the free cash flow and diluted EPS growth rates are both meaningful and above zero, and any forward hard gate is met.
fcf-growth-pass.name: FCF Growth Pass

fcf-growth-strategy.body:
It returns `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `INDETERMINATE`, and it is not an investment recommendation.

Related terms: [total-company FCF](help:terms/total-company-fcf), [FCF per diluted share](help:terms/fcf-per-diluted-share), [weighted-average diluted shares](help:terms/weighted-average-diluted-shares), [operating cash flow](help:terms/operating-cash-flow).
fcf-growth-strategy.definition: A historical screen asking whether free cash flow and diluted EPS both grew at positive, meaningful compound annual rates over one compatible period. It is not a valuation.
fcf-growth-strategy.name: Free Cash Flow & Earnings Growth Strategy

fcf-per-diluted-share.body: It reflects dilution and repurchases and can be selected as the controlling classification basis.
fcf-per-diluted-share.definition: Annual total-company FCF divided by compatible weighted-average diluted shares for the same fiscal year.
fcf-per-diluted-share.name: FCF per Diluted Share

fcf-yield.body: Its numerator covers a completed year and its denominator is taken at the boundary; it is informational only in the current method.
fcf-yield.definition: Latest completed annual free cash flow divided by market capitalization at the boundary, expressed as a percentage.
fcf-yield.name: FCF Yield

financial-facts.definition: Reported accounting values such as earnings, shareholders' equity and shares outstanding, taken from financial statements. Their reporting periods usually differ from market-quote times.
financial-facts.name: Company Financial Facts / Fundamentals

fiscal-year.body: Annual EPS observations must therefore retain their fiscal-period dates.
fiscal-year.definition: A company's twelve-month accounting period, which may differ from the calendar year.
fiscal-year.name: Fiscal Year

forward-evidence-complete.body: See [Forward Evidence Status](help:terms/forward-evidence-status) for the whole set of values.
forward-evidence-complete.definition: The latest actual EPS and both consensus estimates were found, and both growth intervals between them could be calculated.
forward-evidence-complete.name: Complete Forward Evidence

forward-evidence-partial.body: See [Forward Evidence Status](help:terms/forward-evidence-status) for the whole set of values.
forward-evidence-partial.definition: At least one consensus estimate was found, but not enough to calculate both growth intervals.
forward-evidence-partial.name: Partial Forward Evidence

forward-evidence-status.body:
Forward evidence is optional. Whether it can change the result is set by the [forward policy](help:terms/forward-policy). See [analyst consensus estimate](help:terms/analyst-consensus-estimate).

The values are explained in [Complete Forward Evidence](help:terms/forward-evidence-complete), [Partial Forward Evidence](help:terms/forward-evidence-partial), [Unavailable Forward Evidence](help:terms/forward-evidence-unavailable).
forward-evidence-status.definition: How complete the analyst-consensus evidence is: complete when every estimate was found, partial when only some were, unavailable when none was.
forward-evidence-status.name: Forward Evidence Status

forward-evidence-unavailable.body: The engine has no approved source of consensus estimates yet, so this is the usual value. See [Forward Evidence Status](help:terms/forward-evidence-status) for the whole set of values.
forward-evidence-unavailable.definition: No usable consensus estimate was found, so the forward evidence is empty.
forward-evidence-unavailable.name: Unavailable Forward Evidence

forward-policy.body: The code values are `display_only`, `confirmation`, and `hard_gate`. Only `hard_gate` can alter an otherwise passing historical classification.
forward-policy.definition: The rule for how optional analyst-consensus EPS estimates for the next two fiscal years are treated: display only, confirmation or hard gate.
forward-policy.name: Forward Policy

free-cash-flow.body:
In the Free Cash Flow & Earnings Growth strategy, it is completed annual operating cash flow minus normalized capital expenditures.

FCF is a non-GAAP analytical measure, so another provider may use a different definition.
free-cash-flow.definition: The cash a company's operations generate in a year, minus what it spends on long-lived assets such as equipment.
free-cash-flow.name: Free Cash Flow (FCF)

graham-growth-value-strategy.body:
It is independent of the Graham Number: a different strategy with a different formula, not an alternative method of the same one. The growth rate and the yield are assumptions you supply.

Related terms: [Graham growth-value formula](help:terms/growth-value-formula), [growth multiplier](help:terms/growth-multiplier), [base P/E](help:terms/base-pe), [growth-estimation policy](help:terms/growth-estimation-policy), [AAA corporate bond yield](help:terms/aaa-corporate-bond-yield), [baseline AAA yield](help:terms/baseline-aaa-yield), [current AAA yield](help:terms/current-aaa-yield).
graham-growth-value-strategy.definition: A forecast-dependent strategy that estimates a value from earnings, an expected growth rate and a current AAA corporate-bond yield.
graham-growth-value-strategy.name: Graham Growth Value Strategy

graham-number.body:
It is a commonly used algebraic expression of those combined limits:

```text
sqrt(22.5 × EPS × BVPS)
```

The result is a maximum indicated price or screening ceiling when EPS and BVPS are positive. It does not by itself prove that a company satisfies Graham's other defensive-investor criteria or that the stock is a suitable investment.
graham-number.definition: The square root of 22.5 times EPS times BVPS, a price ceiling that expresses Graham's defensive limits of P/E 15 and P/B 1.5.
graham-number.name: Graham Number

graham-number-factor.body: Algebraically, `P/E × P/B = price² / (EPS × BVPS)`, which leads to the square-root formula.
graham-number-factor.definition: The product of the Graham Number's component limits: 15 times 1.5 equals 22.5.
graham-number-factor.name: Factor 22.5

graham-number-strategy.body:
It is independent of Graham Growth Value: a different strategy with a different formula, not an alternative method of the same one.

Related terms: [Graham Number factor](help:terms/graham-number-factor), [defensive investor](help:terms/defensive-investor).
graham-number-strategy.definition: A screening strategy that combines positive earnings per share and book value per share to estimate a conservative maximum indicated price.
graham-number-strategy.name: Graham Number Strategy

gross-margin.definition: Gross profit divided by sales for a fiscal year.
gross-margin.name: Gross Margin

growth-estimation-policy.body: An LLM, data provider, or silent default must not invent growth.
growth-estimation-policy.definition: The explicit rule that supplies the expected growth rate. The application supports only a growth assumption that you provide.
growth-estimation-policy.name: Growth-Estimation Policy

growth-multiplier.definition: The configurable constant that multiplies the expected growth rate in the growth-value formula.
growth-multiplier.name: Growth Multiplier

growth-trend.body:
The trend is evidence and not a score. Both growing and neither growing mean what they say. Free cash flow growing without earnings, or earnings growing without free cash flow, names the one that grew. The last value means a growth rate could not be calculated meaningfully. See [free cash flow](help:terms/free-cash-flow) and [CAGR](help:terms/cagr).

The values are explained in [Both Growing](help:terms/growth-trend-both), [Only Free Cash Flow Growing](help:terms/growth-trend-fcf-only), [Only Earnings Growing](help:terms/growth-trend-earnings-only), [Neither Growing](help:terms/growth-trend-neither), [Insufficient Growth Evidence](help:terms/growth-trend-insufficient).
growth-trend.definition: How free cash flow growth and earnings growth compare over the screened period: both growing, only one growing, neither growing, or too little meaningful data to say.
growth-trend.name: Growth Trend

growth-trend-both.body: See [Growth Trend](help:terms/growth-trend) for the whole set of values.
growth-trend-both.definition: Free cash flow and diluted EPS both increased over the measured period.
growth-trend-both.name: Both Growing

growth-trend-earnings-only.body: See [Growth Trend](help:terms/growth-trend) for the whole set of values.
growth-trend-earnings-only.definition: Diluted EPS increased over the measured period, but free cash flow did not.
growth-trend-earnings-only.name: Only Earnings Growing

growth-trend-fcf-only.body: See [Growth Trend](help:terms/growth-trend) for the whole set of values.
growth-trend-fcf-only.definition: Free cash flow increased over the measured period, but diluted EPS did not.
growth-trend-fcf-only.name: Only Free Cash Flow Growing

growth-trend-insufficient.body: Without both rates the engine cannot say which of the two grew. See [Growth Trend](help:terms/growth-trend) for the whole set of values.
growth-trend-insufficient.definition: At least one of the two growth rates, of free cash flow and of diluted EPS, could not be calculated or is not meaningful, so the trend cannot be described.
growth-trend-insufficient.name: Insufficient Growth Evidence

growth-trend-neither.body: See [Growth Trend](help:terms/growth-trend) for the whole set of values.
growth-trend-neither.definition: Neither free cash flow nor diluted EPS increased over the measured period.
growth-trend-neither.name: Neither Growing

growth-value-formula.body:
The project's explicitly identified secondary convention:

```text
normalized_eps × (base_pe + growth_multiplier × g)
× baseline_aaa_yield / current_aaa_yield
```

It is a simplified, forecast-dependent growth-stock estimate. It is not the Graham Number and must not be presented as a precise or universally applicable intrinsic value.
growth-value-formula.definition: The project's secondary valuation formula: earnings scaled by a growth-adjusted multiple and by the ratio of baseline to current AAA yield. It is a simplified estimate that depends on a forecast.
growth-value-formula.name: Graham Growth-Value Formula

headline.body: A value the run could not calculate is shown as a dash.
headline.definition: The few values a strategy picks to stand for one analysis run, so that runs can be compared side by side. It summarizes the run; it is not the full result.
headline.name: Headline

headline-unavailable.body:
A run stored under an older version is kept but not read by this version. A run of a strategy that is no longer available shows only its outcome. A run that stored no result has an outcome but nothing to summarize. The comparison shows a dash for the missing cells.

Related terms: [headline](help:terms/headline).
headline-unavailable.definition: The reason a saved run has no headline in a side-by-side comparison: it was stored under an older version, its strategy is no longer available, or it stored no result.
headline-unavailable.name: Headline Unavailable

historical-horizon.body: The default picks the longest history available, up to five years. A longer horizon needs more consecutive annual facts and is unavailable when there are too few.
historical-horizon.definition: The number of elapsed years of history the growth screen looks back over: three, four or five, or the longest available.
historical-horizon.name: Historical Horizon

historical-market-data.definition: A time-indexed series of market observations, such as daily prices, used for time-series calculations such as Momentum.
historical-market-data.name: Historical Market Data

industry-class.body: It comes from the [as-filed SIC code](help:terms/as-filed-sic-code) of the annual report the analysis rests on. The groups are financial (SIC 6000 to 6799, which includes REITs), utility (4900 to 4999), manufacturer (2000 to 3999), or any other issuer. A strategy that does not apply to a class reports the issuer as not applicable; a strategy that depends on the class reports an unknown class as unavailable, and one that does not (Piotroski) runs and says the class is unknown. The SEC assigns one code per filer, so a diversified issuer has the class of that one code.
industry-class.definition: The group an issuer belongs to for deciding which screening strategies apply: financial, utility, manufacturer or other. It is unknown when the issuer's industry code cannot be established.
industry-class.name: Industry Class

instrument-kind.body: A strategy that is built for company financial statements reports an instrument kind it does not cover as not applicable. See [instrument profile](help:terms/instrument-profile).
instrument-kind.definition: The kind of security a ticker names: an equity, an exchange-traded fund or a cryptocurrency.
instrument-kind.name: Instrument Kind

instrument-profile.body: The engine keeps a durable copy of an instrument profile; a stored profile expires after a configured freshness window and is refreshed live when it does. If a refresh finds a genuinely different entity behind the same ticker — a **ticker reuse**, such as a delisting followed by a new listing under the same symbol — the prior profile is retired rather than overwritten, and every Analysis Run that already used it keeps showing that original entity: reopening an old result never relabels it using the ticker's current meaning.
instrument-profile.definition: A security's identity plus a normalized kind of instrument, such as equity or ETF, each with its own provenance. It is kept so that repeated analyses do not look up details that rarely change.
instrument-profile.name: Instrument Profile

intrinsic-value.body: Different models can produce different intrinsic-value estimates. Investment Analysis Engine avoids using this term without qualification for the Graham Number.
intrinsic-value.definition: An estimate of what an investment is economically worth under a stated model and assumptions, rather than its market price.
intrinsic-value.name: Intrinsic Value

invested-capital.body: Net working capital here excludes cash, short-term investments and the debt in current liabilities.
invested-capital.definition: The tangible capital employed: net working capital plus net property, plant and equipment, with goodwill and intangibles excluded.
invested-capital.name: Invested Capital

look-ahead-bias.body: Tracking availability dates separately from reporting periods helps prevent it.
look-ahead-bias.definition: An error in historical analysis caused by using information that was not yet available at the analysis date.
look-ahead-bias.name: Look-Ahead Bias

macd.body: It is not currently part of the implemented Momentum calculation.
macd.definition: A trend and momentum indicator built from the relationship between exponential moving averages.
macd.name: MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence)

macro-series.body: A specific observation must retain its series identifier, units, source and observation date.
macro-series.definition: A time-indexed economic or market benchmark, such as a corporate-bond-yield series.
macro-series.name: Macro Series

margin-of-safety.body:
```text
(reference_value - current_price) / reference_value × 100
```

Negative means the price is above the reference value. This calculation measures a valuation discount or premium but does not eliminate business or investment risk. If the reference value or current price is unavailable, MOS is unavailable (`None`), not zero.
margin-of-safety.definition: The percentage difference between a method's reference value and the current market price, measured against the reference value. Positive means the price is below the reference value.
margin-of-safety.name: Margin of Safety (MOS)

market-capitalization.body: The share count is scaled by every stock split after the date it was taken, and the price is the split-adjusted close. It is available only for an issuer whose annual filing is a 10-K, whose quote currency equals its filing currency, and whose listing on the filing's cover page is a share of the issuer. See [Financial Math](help:documents/finance-math#shared-metrics).
market-capitalization.definition: Common shares outstanding multiplied by the share price, both on the basis of the same date.
market-capitalization.name: Market Capitalization

maximum-indicated-price.body: This is the preferred description of the Graham Number result.
maximum-indicated-price.definition: The highest price indicated by the Graham Number's limited earnings-and-book-value screen. It is not a promise of fair value or future return.
maximum-indicated-price.name: Maximum Indicated Price / Screening Ceiling

method.body:
Several methods in one strategy are reserved for true variants of the same underlying calculation, such as a future Altman Z versus Z′′ strategy. They are not for strategies that merely address a related question with a different formula, the way Graham Number and Graham Growth Value do: each of those is its own strategy, not two methods of one.

A method is an application concept; it does not imply that Benjamin Graham or another source used the word “method” in exactly this project-specific sense.

Related terms: [analysis strategy](help:terms/analysis-strategy).
method.definition: One calculation approach within an analysis strategy. A strategy may offer one method or several.
method.name: Method

momentum-states.body:
The run's status is then `input_unavailable`.

The values are explained in [Bullish Trend](help:terms/trend-bullish), [Bearish Trend](help:terms/trend-bearish), [Unknown Trend](help:terms/trend-unknown).
momentum-states.definition: The trend a Momentum run reports: bullish when the short moving average is above the long one, bearish when it is not, unknown when they cannot be calculated.
momentum-states.name: Bullish / Bearish / Unknown

momentum-strategy.body:
The moving-average windows are configurable. The strategy reports the state of the crossover of the two averages.

Related terms: [historical market data](help:terms/historical-market-data), [EMA](help:terms/ema).
momentum-strategy.definition: A rule-based analysis of recent price behavior. It compares a short and a long simple moving average, reports a bullish or bearish trend, and shows RSI as a supporting indicator.
momentum-strategy.name: Momentum Strategy

net-dilution.body: The F-Score's dilution test passes when the count did not rise.
net-dilution.definition: The change in the number of common shares outstanding between two fiscal year-ends, after buybacks.
net-dilution.name: Net Dilution

normalized-eps.body: “Normalized” is not self-defining: every adjustment and period must be documented. The growth calculator accepts an EPS value on the explicitly selected basis; the software does not invent discretionary normalization adjustments.
normalized-eps.definition: Earnings adjusted by an explicit policy to reduce the effect of unusual or non-recurring items.
normalized-eps.name: Normalized EPS / Normal Earnings

not-applicable.body: The code value is `not_applicable`. It is not the same as a software failure or a zero valuation.
not-applicable.definition: A valid outcome meaning the method should not be used for the supplied facts, for example when earnings or book value per share is not positive.
not-applicable.name: Not Applicable

operating-cash-flow.body: It is the starting component in the project's free-cash-flow calculation.
operating-cash-flow.definition: Net cash provided by operating activities for a completed fiscal year.
operating-cash-flow.name: Operating Cash Flow (OCF)

outcome-completed.body: It is the outcome of a run whose calculation status is [ok](help:terms/status-ok). It says that a result exists, not that the result is favorable: a screen can complete and still report that a company failed it.
outcome-completed.definition: A run outcome meaning the strategy calculated its result from the inputs it was given.
outcome-completed.name: Completed Run

outcome-failed.body: It is the outcome of a run whose calculation status is [invalid input](help:terms/status-invalid-input) or [provider error](help:terms/status-provider-error). The run's failure code says which.
outcome-failed.definition: A run outcome meaning the analysis stopped because an input was invalid or a data provider failed. No result was produced.
outcome-failed.name: Failed Run

outcome-unavailable.body: It is the outcome of a run whose calculation status is [input unavailable](help:terms/status-input-unavailable). The run is saved so that it can be revisited; nothing is estimated or replaced by zero.
outcome-unavailable.definition: A run outcome meaning the analysis could not be calculated because an input it needs was not available.
outcome-unavailable.name: Unavailable Run

override.definition: A value you supply yourself instead of accepting the value found from the cache or a provider. An override takes precedence over every other source and is identified in provenance.
override.name: Override

pb-ratio.definition: Share price divided by book value per share. A P/B of 1.5 means the price is one and one-half times BVPS.
pb-ratio.name: P/B (Price-to-Book Ratio)

pe-ratio.definition: Share price divided by earnings per share. A P/E of 15 means the price is fifteen times the selected EPS measure.
pe-ratio.name: P/E (Price-to-Earnings Ratio)

percentage-point.body: That is a 50% increase relative to the original 4%.
percentage-point.definition: The arithmetic difference between two percentages. Moving from 4% to 6% is an increase of 2 percentage points.
percentage-point.name: Percentage Point

period-kind.body: A completed annual fact covers one fiscal year. A quarterly fact covers one quarter, and a trailing-twelve-month fact covers the twelve months ending at a quarter. An instant fact is a balance measured on one date, such as a share count or total debt. A calculation uses only the kind its method needs. See [reporting period](help:terms/reporting-period) and [TTM](help:terms/ttm).
period-kind.definition: The kind of reporting period behind a financial fact: a completed fiscal year, a quarter, the trailing twelve months, or a single instant.
period-kind.name: Period Kind

piotroski-strategy.body:
It follows the Piotroski nine-test structure but substitutes the net change in split-adjusted shares outstanding for the original equity-issuance signal. It is not an investment recommendation.

Related terms: [ROA](help:terms/roa), [current ratio](help:terms/current-ratio), [gross margin](help:terms/gross-margin), [asset turnover](help:terms/asset-turnover), [net dilution](help:terms/net-dilution).
piotroski-strategy.definition: A financial-strength screen that runs nine pass/fail tests on three consecutive fiscal years of reported statements and counts those passed. It is not a valuation.
piotroski-strategy.name: Piotroski F-Score Strategy

price-basis.body: The basis shows which price series the averages and the RSI were calculated from. Providers revise adjusted prices after the fact, so an adjusted close can differ from the price quoted on that day.
price-basis.definition: Which close the current price is: the latest adjusted historical close, or the latest historical close without the adjustment.
price-basis.name: Price Basis

price-comparison-available.body: See [Price Comparison Status](help:terms/price-comparison-status) for the whole set of values.
price-comparison-available.definition: The method's value could be compared with the price, so a margin of safety was calculated.
price-comparison-available.name: Price Comparison Available

price-comparison-status.body:
An unavailable comparison leaves the [margin of safety](help:terms/margin-of-safety) without a value; it is never replaced by zero. See [price relationship](help:terms/price-relationship).

The values are explained in [Price Comparison Available](help:terms/price-comparison-available), [Price Comparison Unavailable](help:terms/price-comparison-unavailable).
price-comparison-status.definition: Whether a comparison between a method's value and the price could be made: available when it could, unavailable when it could not.
price-comparison-status.name: Price Comparison Status

price-comparison-unavailable.body: See [Price Comparison Status](help:terms/price-comparison-status) for the whole set of values.
price-comparison-unavailable.definition: The method's value could not be compared with the price, so no margin of safety is shown.
price-comparison-unavailable.name: Price Comparison Unavailable

price-relationship.body:
It avoids requiring you to interpret the sign convention of the stored `margin_of_safety_percent` field. Another example is “89.57% above the Graham growth value.”

Related terms: [discount and premium](help:terms/discount-and-premium), [percentage point](help:terms/percentage-point).
price-relationship.definition: A plain-language statement of how the market price compares with the reference value, such as 20.00% below the Graham Number.
price-relationship.name: Price Relationship

provenance.body: Provenance can include source kind, provider, source field, observation period, retrieval time, calculation steps, and whether the value was overridden.
provenance.definition: The record of where a value came from and how it was transformed.
provenance.name: Provenance

provider-healthy.body: The check is made after a failure to tell a provider problem from a problem with one ticker. See [data provider](help:terms/data-provider).
provider-healthy.definition: A test request to the data provider was answered normally.
provider-healthy.name: Provider Healthy

provider-no-data.body: Unlike an unreachable provider, the provider worked; it holds no data for what was asked.
provider-no-data.definition: The data provider answered correctly and has nothing for this request.
provider-no-data.name: Provider Returned No Data

provider-not-checked.body: A provider is checked only when a failure suggests a problem with it.
provider-not-checked.definition: No test request was made to the data provider, so nothing is known about its condition.
provider-not-checked.name: Provider Not Checked

provider-rate-limited.body: The analysis can be tried again after a pause.
provider-rate-limited.definition: The data provider refused the request because it is limiting how many requests it accepts.
provider-rate-limited.name: Provider Rate-Limited

provider-unexpected-response.body: The provider may have changed its format. Nothing in the answer is used.
provider-unexpected-response.definition: The data provider answered, but not in a form the engine reads, so the answer could not be used.
provider-unexpected-response.name: Provider Unexpected Response

provider-unreachable.body: It says nothing about whether the data exists. The same request can succeed later.
provider-unreachable.definition: The data provider did not serve the request, because of a connection problem, a timeout, a block or a server error.
provider-unreachable.name: Provider Unreachable

quote-expired.body: See [Quote Freshness](help:terms/quote-freshness) for the whole set of values.
quote-expired.definition: A quote retrieved longer ago than the freshness limit, so it is no longer treated as current.
quote-expired.name: Expired Quote

quote-freshness.body:
A recently retrieved quote is younger than the freshness limit and an expired quote is older. A quote with no recorded retrieval time is unknown, and one dated after the time of the analysis is a future timestamp. A quote you supplied as an override is user supplied. A quote read for a past as-of date is historical. See [current quote](help:terms/current-quote) and [retrieved at](help:terms/retrieved-at).

The values are explained in [Recently Retrieved Quote](help:terms/quote-recent), [Expired Quote](help:terms/quote-expired), [Quote With Unknown Retrieval Time](help:terms/quote-retrieval-unknown), [Future-Dated Quote](help:terms/quote-future-timestamp), [User-Supplied Quote](help:terms/quote-user-supplied), [Historical Quote](help:terms/quote-historical).
quote-freshness.definition: How recent the price quote behind a comparison is: recently retrieved, expired, of unknown retrieval time, dated in the future, supplied by you, or historical.
quote-freshness.name: Quote Freshness

quote-future-timestamp.body: See [Quote Freshness](help:terms/quote-freshness) for the whole set of values.
quote-future-timestamp.definition: The quote's retrieval or market time is later than the time of the analysis, so its freshness cannot be judged.
quote-future-timestamp.name: Future-Dated Quote

quote-historical.body: See [Quote Freshness](help:terms/quote-freshness) for the whole set of values.
quote-historical.definition: The price was read for a past as-of date and not as a current quote, so no freshness limit applies.
quote-historical.name: Historical Quote

quote-recent.body: See [Quote Freshness](help:terms/quote-freshness) for the whole set of values.
quote-recent.definition: A quote retrieved within the freshness limit, so it is treated as current.
quote-recent.name: Recently Retrieved Quote

quote-retrieval-unknown.body: See [Quote Freshness](help:terms/quote-freshness) for the whole set of values.
quote-retrieval-unknown.definition: No retrieval time was recorded for the quote, so its age cannot be judged.
quote-retrieval-unknown.name: Quote With Unknown Retrieval Time

quote-user-supplied.body: See [Quote Freshness](help:terms/quote-freshness) for the whole set of values.
quote-user-supplied.definition: The price was supplied as an override, so no retrieval age applies.
quote-user-supplied.name: User-Supplied Quote

reason-ambiguous-fact.body: Choosing one would be a guess. The value stays unavailable.
reason-ambiguous-fact.definition: Facts conflict, or a fact cannot be identified reliably, so the engine chooses none of them.
reason-ambiguous-fact.name: Ambiguous Fact

reason-debt-not-visible.body: An absent debt component counts as zero only when nothing related to it is tagged. Otherwise total debt is unavailable. See [total debt](help:terms/total-debt).
reason-debt-not-visible.definition: Total debt cannot be determined from the filing: related debt is tagged but no usable component is shown, or the filing's debt mapping is not supported.
reason-debt-not-visible.name: Debt Not Visible

reason-earlier-basis.body: The restated years and the older years are on different bases, so the engine never combines them and does no split arithmetic to convert one to the other. It uses the newest run of years that share one basis and names the years it left out. A year whose filings, filed together, give different values is left out too, with the reason [ambiguous fact](help:terms/reason-ambiguous-fact), and so is every year older than it. When a requested history needs those years, the result is indeterminate with this reason. See [stock split adjustment](help:terms/stock-split-adjustment) and [fiscal year](help:terms/fiscal-year).
reason-earlier-basis.definition: A year is left out because the company reported it only before a later filing restated other years, for example after a stock split.
reason-earlier-basis.name: Earlier Basis

reason-forward-not-confirmed.definition: The analyst consensus does not confirm the historical growth, which counts when the forward policy requires confirmation.
reason-forward-not-confirmed.name: Forward Growth Not Confirmed

reason-growth-not-meaningful.body: A compound growth rate needs a positive start and a positive end. See [CAGR](help:terms/cagr).
reason-growth-not-meaningful.definition: A growth rate or ratio cannot be calculated meaningfully, because a base value is zero or negative or the sign changed across the period.
reason-growth-not-meaningful.name: Growth Not Meaningful

reason-incompatible-inputs.body: A scope can be the accounting scope or the filing taxonomy. The engine does not convert or substitute to make the inputs fit. See [period kind](help:terms/period-kind), [accounting scope](help:terms/accounting-scope) and [reporting currency](help:terms/reporting-currency).
reason-incompatible-inputs.definition: Two inputs cannot be combined because their reporting periods, units, currencies or scopes differ.
reason-incompatible-inputs.name: Incompatible Inputs

reason-industry-class-unknown.body: The class comes from the as-filed SIC code. See [industry class](help:terms/industry-class) and [as-filed SIC code](help:terms/as-filed-sic-code).
reason-industry-class-unknown.definition: The issuer's industry class could not be established, so the strategy could not decide whether it applies.
reason-industry-class-unknown.name: Industry Class Unknown

reason-insufficient-history.body: Too few observations are not filled in, and a gap is not bridged. The value stays unavailable.
reason-insufficient-history.definition: The history does not cover enough periods for the calculation, or its periods are not consecutive.
reason-insufficient-history.name: Insufficient History

reason-insufficient-tests.definition: Fewer than six of the nine tests could be decided, so no score is given.
reason-insufficient-tests.name: Insufficient Tests

reason-invalid-request.body: The metric is reported as not applicable. See [not applicable](help:terms/not-applicable).
reason-invalid-request.definition: A metric was asked for with an invalid input, or its result is too large to represent, so it is not calculated.
reason-invalid-request.name: Invalid Request

reason-missing-input.body: The missing input can be a reported fact, the analyst consensus or the market capitalization. A missing figure is never replaced by zero.
reason-missing-input.definition: A fact or an input the calculation needs is missing, so the value is not calculated rather than assumed.
reason-missing-input.name: Missing Input

reason-not-available-as-of.body: The engine never uses information from after the boundary. See [as-of date](help:terms/as-of-date) and [look-ahead bias](help:terms/look-ahead-bias).
reason-not-available-as-of.definition: An input was not yet available on the as-of date, for example because it was filed or published after it.
reason-not-available-as-of.name: Not Available As Of

reason-not-growing.body: The code says which of the two did not grow. See [FCF classification](help:terms/fcf-classification).
reason-not-growing.definition: A required growth rate is not positive, so a growth screen does not pass: free cash flow, earnings or both did not grow.
reason-not-growing.name: Not Growing

reason-security-not-applicable.body: A strategy built for company financial statements does not cover every instrument or every industry. See [instrument kind](help:terms/instrument-kind), [industry class](help:terms/industry-class) and [not applicable](help:terms/not-applicable).
reason-security-not-applicable.definition: The strategy does not apply to this kind of security or to its industry class.
reason-security-not-applicable.name: Security Not Applicable

reason-stale-anchor.body: The share count in that report is not the count at the as-of date. The run keeps its status and a warning states the fiscal year, the form and the date the next report was due. See [anchor filing](help:terms/anchor-filing).
reason-stale-anchor.definition: The market capitalization is not calculated: the newest annual report was overdue for replacement at the as-of date and none was filed.
reason-stale-anchor.name: Stale Anchor

reference-value.body: The stored names are `maximum_indicated_price` for the Graham Number and `growth_value` for Graham Growth Value.
reference-value.definition: The value a method produces for comparison with the current price, such as the Graham Number's maximum indicated price or the growth value.
reference-value.name: Reference Value

refresh.body: A refresh limits how many tickers run at once, and one ticker's failure never stops the rest of the watchlist.
refresh.definition: Running every entry in one watchlist and saving each result as its own analysis run.
refresh.name: Refresh

refresh-event.body: A finished event carries the entry's result. A refresh runs one entry at a time or several at once, so events of different entries can interleave.
refresh-event.definition: A progress record of a refresh: one is recorded when an entry starts running and one when it finishes.
refresh-event.name: Refresh Event

reporting-currency.body: A method that combines figures with a price needs the filing currency and the quote currency to agree. A selection can require annual facts in one reporting currency.
reporting-currency.definition: The currency a company states its financial figures in, written as a three-letter ISO 4217 code such as USD.
reporting-currency.name: Reporting Currency

reporting-period.definition: The span or date a financial fact applies to, such as a fiscal year, a quarter, a trailing twelve-month interval or a balance-sheet date.
reporting-period.name: Reporting Period

resolution-precedence.definition: The order in which sources are tried for each financial value: your override, then a valid cache entry, then a configured provider, then an explicit statement that the value is unavailable.
resolution-precedence.name: Resolution Precedence

retrieved-at.definition: The time the application obtained a value. It differs from the as-of date: an old financial statement can be retrieved today and still keep its historical reporting date.
retrieved-at.name: Retrieval Time

roa.definition: In the F-Score, a year's net income divided by total assets at the start of that year.
roa.name: ROA (Return on Assets)

rsi.body: The Momentum strategy uses a simple trailing-average RSI, with a default period of 14 price changes; it does not use Wilder smoothing. See [Financial Math](help:documents/finance-math#momentum-strategy) for the formula and zero-loss/flat-window conventions.
rsi.definition: An indicator from 0 to 100 that compares the size of recent price gains with recent losses.
rsi.name: RSI (Relative Strength Index)

score-complete.body: See [Complete Score / Partial Score](help:terms/complete-and-partial-score) for the whole set of values.
score-complete.definition: A score that rests on all nine tests.
score-complete.name: Complete Score

score-partial.body: See [Complete Score / Partial Score](help:terms/complete-and-partial-score) for the whole set of values.
score-partial.definition: A score that rests on six to eight tests, because the others are unavailable.
score-partial.name: Partial Score

sec.definition: The United States Securities and Exchange Commission, the federal securities regulator. The engine uses its public data as a source of company financial facts.
sec.name: SEC

security-identity.body: Security identity is best-effort metadata recorded at a resolution time. A ticker is not permanent identity and may be reused. Missing identity metadata never changes a financial result, and historical Analysis Runs retain their original identity snapshot rather than silently re-resolving the ticker later.
security-identity.definition: Descriptive details that associate a ticker with an instrument name and, when known, its listing venue and issuer identifiers. They never change a financial result.
security-identity.name: Security Identity

selection.body: The same method may appear in more than one selection, for example to compare Graham Number computed from SEC EDGAR data under two different overrides.
selection.definition: One analysis method together with its own configuration, such as Graham Number with SEC EDGAR data or Graham Growth Value with a 6% expected-growth assumption.
