selection.name: Selection

share-count-basis.body: The year-end count is preferred. The cover-page count is used only when no balance-sheet path gives a count at the year-end, and the result says so. See [shares outstanding](help:terms/shares-outstanding) and [market capitalization](help:terms/market-capitalization).
share-count-basis.definition: Where a share count was taken from: the balance sheet at the fiscal year-end, or the cover page of the annual filing.
share-count-basis.name: Share-Count Basis

shares-outstanding.body: This period-end figure is commonly used when deriving BVPS and differs from weighted-average shares used in EPS.
shares-outstanding.definition: The number of issued common shares held by investors, usually measured at a reporting date.
shares-outstanding.name: Shares Outstanding

sma.definition: The arithmetic mean of a price series over a rolling window.
sma.name: SMA (Simple Moving Average)

sma-windows.definition: The two averaging periods that are compared: the short window and the long window. The short window must be shorter than the long window.
sma-windows.name: Short Window / Long Window

source-kind.body:
The source is kept with every input so that a saved run can show where each figure came from. See [override](help:terms/override), [cache](help:terms/cache) and [provenance](help:terms/provenance).

Related terms: [resolution precedence](help:terms/resolution-precedence), [financial facts](help:terms/financial-facts), [macro series](help:terms/macro-series).
source-kind.definition: How a resolved input value was obtained: you supplied it as an override, it came from the cache, it was fetched from a data provider, or the engine derived it from other inputs.
source-kind.name: Input Source

split-adjusted-close.body: It is the price on the same basis as a share count scaled by those splits, and the two together give the market capitalization the shares and the price had on the day. It is not the dividend-adjusted close that the [Momentum](help:terms/momentum-strategy) series uses. A stock dividend appears in the provider's split history as a fractional split (1.05) and is treated like a split; it is not counted as new shares issued.
split-adjusted-close.definition: A closing price restated for every stock split after its date, and for nothing else. A dividend paid later does not change it.
split-adjusted-close.name: Split-Adjusted Close

split-adjustment-window.body: A recognizable split between the share count and the price is applied to the share count. An adjustment after the price date is always applied, because it undoes the provider's adjustment of the historical close. See [stock split adjustment](help:terms/stock-split-adjustment) and [market capitalization](help:terms/market-capitalization).
split-adjustment-window.definition: Where a data provider's adjustment fell relative to the share count and the price: between the count and the price, or between the price and the date the provider adjusted to.
split-adjustment-window.name: Split-Adjustment Window

status-input-unavailable.body: It is the calculation status of an [unavailable run](help:terms/outcome-unavailable). It is also the category of a failure whose data could not be used, such as a data-quality failure, a lack of observations or a provider that did not deliver.
status-input-unavailable.definition: A required input could not be found for the date and the data the analysis was asked to use. The analysis is not calculated rather than guessed.
status-input-unavailable.name: Input Unavailable

status-invalid-input.body: It is the calculation status that makes a run [failed](help:terms/outcome-failed), and the failure code of the same name. The shown message says only that the inputs or the provider data were invalid; the details are kept in the engine's log.
status-invalid-input.definition: A value given to the analysis, or read from provider data, is not valid, so the analysis cannot be calculated.
status-invalid-input.name: Invalid Input

status-ok.body: It is the calculation status that gives a run the outcome [completed](help:terms/outcome-completed). For a single metric it means the metric has a value.
status-ok.definition: The calculation finished: every required input was found and the value could be calculated.
status-ok.name: OK Status

status-provider-error.body: It is the calculation status that makes a run [failed](help:terms/outcome-failed). The failure code of the same name is used when the provider's failure could not be classified; a classified failure has its own entry: [unreachable](help:terms/provider-unreachable), [rate-limited](help:terms/provider-rate-limited), [unexpected response](help:terms/provider-unexpected-response) or [no data](help:terms/provider-no-data).
status-provider-error.definition: A data provider failed in a way that is not an absent fact, so the analysis could not be calculated.
status-provider-error.name: Provider Error

status-unavailable.body: A metric that is unavailable usually comes with a reason code that says why. See [Applicability Status](help:terms/applicability-status).
status-unavailable.definition: A single metric that could not be calculated, usually because an input it needs is missing. It shows no value, and nothing takes its place.
status-unavailable.name: Unavailable Metric

stock-split-adjustment.body:
EPS, BVPS, and price must use compatible share bases.

Related terms: [split-adjusted close](help:terms/split-adjusted-close).
stock-split-adjustment.definition: Restating per-share values after the number of shares changes through a stock split or reverse split.
stock-split-adjustment.name: Stock Split Adjustment

tangible-book-value.body: It is a distinct variation and must never be silently substituted for ordinary book value or BVPS.
tangible-book-value.definition: Book value after subtracting goodwill and other intangible assets, in total or per share.
tangible-book-value.name: Tangible Book Value / Tangible BVPS

test-failed.body: See [Test Result](help:terms/test-result) for the whole set of values.
test-failed.definition: A Piotroski F-Score test whose condition does not hold. It adds nothing to the score.
test-failed.name: Failed Test

test-passed.body: See [Test Result](help:terms/test-result) for the whole set of values.
test-passed.definition: A Piotroski F-Score test whose condition holds. It adds one point to the score.
test-passed.name: Passed Test

test-result.body:
A test that cannot be decided is not a fail; it is an [unavailable test](help:terms/unavailable-test). The [F-Score](help:terms/f-score) counts the passes.

The values are explained in [Passed Test](help:terms/test-passed), [Failed Test](help:terms/test-failed).
test-result.definition: The result of one test of the score: a pass when its condition holds and a fail when it does not.
test-result.name: Test Result

three-year-average-eps.body: Investment Analysis Engine uses this as the standard Graham Number earnings basis and when the Graham Growth Value strategy uses SEC EDGAR earnings data, reflecting Graham's defensive-investor emphasis on average earnings over the preceding three years.
three-year-average-eps.definition: The arithmetic mean of EPS from three completed fiscal years.
three-year-average-eps.name: Three-Year-Average EPS

ticker.body: A ticker is not permanent identity: it can be reassigned after a delisting (see [Security Identity](help:terms/security-identity)).
ticker.definition: The short symbol that identifies a security on an exchange, such as KO for The Coca-Cola Company.
ticker.name: Ticker

total-company-fcf.definition: Free cash flow measured for the company as a whole. Its CAGR is the default classification basis.
total-company-fcf.name: Total-Company FCF

total-debt.body: A missing debt figure is never assumed to be zero without evidence that the filer has none.
total-debt.definition: Short-term borrowings, the current portion of long-term debt, noncurrent long-term debt and the lease liabilities counted as debt.
total-debt.name: Total Debt

trend-bearish.body: The averages can be equal, which is also read as bearish. See [Bullish / Bearish / Unknown](help:terms/momentum-states) for the whole set of values.
trend-bearish.definition: The short moving average is not above the long one at the latest observation, so the trend is read as bearish.
trend-bearish.name: Bearish Trend

trend-bullish.body: Only the latest observation counts; a bullish trend is not a new crossover. See [Bullish / Bearish / Unknown](help:terms/momentum-states) for the whole set of values.
trend-bullish.definition: The short moving average is above the long one at the latest observation, so the trend is read as bullish.
trend-bullish.name: Bullish Trend

trend-relationship.body: Above is the bullish reading of the [trend](help:terms/momentum-states); below or equal is the bearish reading. The relationship describes the latest observation, and a [crossover](help:terms/crossover) describes a change in it.
trend-relationship.definition: How the short moving average stands against the long one: above it, below it or equal to it.
trend-relationship.name: Trend Relationship

trend-unknown.body: The run's status is then input unavailable. See [Bullish / Bearish / Unknown](help:terms/momentum-states) for the whole set of values.
trend-unknown.definition: The trend could not be calculated, because the moving averages are not available.
trend-unknown.name: Unknown Trend

ttm.body: TTM EPS is a current-looking accounting measure but is not the same as one completed fiscal year's EPS or Graham's three-year average. No data source the application currently ships supplies it; the Graham strategies use three-year-average or fiscal-year EPS.
ttm.definition: The most recent continuous twelve-month period covered by available reports.
ttm.name: TTM (Trailing Twelve Months)

typed-evidence.body: “Typed evidence” is distinct from free-form model prose: an AI model may reason about it, but the model does not get to silently redefine or invent the underlying financial values.
typed-evidence.definition: Information with named fields and stated data types, such as a value together with its units, source and dates. It is the opposite of free-form text.
typed-evidence.name: Typed Evidence

unavailable-test.definition: A Piotroski test that cannot be decided because an input is missing or incompatible. It is never counted as a fail.
unavailable-test.name: Unavailable Test

utc.definition: The common time standard used for unambiguous timestamps across systems and time zones.
utc.name: UTC (Coordinated Universal Time)

valuation.body:
In Investment Analysis Engine a valuation result is one method's reference value, such as the Graham Number's maximum indicated price, not a complete intrinsic-value conclusion or a recommendation (see [Intrinsic Value](help:terms/intrinsic-value) and [Reference Value](help:terms/reference-value)).

Related terms: [book value](help:terms/book-value), [tangible book value](help:terms/tangible-book-value), [common shareholders' equity](help:terms/common-shareholders-equity), [EBITDA](help:terms/ebitda), [enterprise value](help:terms/enterprise-value), [invested capital](help:terms/invested-capital), [normalized EPS](help:terms/normalized-eps).
valuation.definition: Estimating what a security may be worth under a stated method and assumptions, usually to compare with its market price.
valuation.name: Valuation

watchlist.body:
Each entry pairs a [ticker](help:terms/ticker) with a [selection](help:terms/selection).

Related terms: [entry](help:terms/entry).
watchlist.definition: A named, ordered list of entries that you want to run and revisit as a group.
watchlist.name: Watchlist

weighted-average-diluted-shares.body: It is not interchangeable with an ending shares-outstanding snapshot.
weighted-average-diluted-shares.definition: The average diluted share count for an earnings period, including the effect of potentially dilutive securities under the reported accounting basis.
weighted-average-diluted-shares.name: Weighted-Average Diluted Shares

yield.definition: Annual income from a bond or other instrument as a percentage of its price or value. A yield is a rate, not a dollar amount.
yield.name: Yield
